chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqṭīnī, from Muhammad ibn Ismā'īl al-Baṣrī, from whoever narrated it from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
The sanctuary of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is one farsakh by one farsakh from the four sides of the grave.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), the third Shia Imam.
key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: The grave, referring specifically to the burial place of the Imam.
key_terms.حَرُمُ: The sanctuary or sacred precinct; a place where specific prohibitions or reverence apply.
key_terms.فَرْسَخٌ: A farsakh, a traditional unit of distance approximately equal to 3.5 to 6 kilometers depending on the school.

ai.seo_question: What are the defined boundaries of Imam Husayn's sanctuary in Karbala?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* precisely delineates the sacred precinct (Ḥaram) of Imam al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) as extending one farsakh in all cardinal directions from his grave, a measurement crucial for determining the validity of specific ritual acts like prayer and tawassul. In Shia jurisprudence, this defined boundary distinguishes the inner sanctum where special virtues apply from the broader Karbala region, reinforcing the theological significance of the site as a focal point for divine grace and pilgrimage.
